property_summary: Calling setSlopes with a kink outside the open interval (0, 1e27) always reverts, while calling it with a valid kink never reverts and updates the event-relevant storage.
Calling setSlopes with a kink of 0 or >= 1e27 always reverts, while any kink in the open interval (0, 1e27) never reverts.
setSlopes reverts exactly when the kink is zero or not less than 1e27, and never reverts for a kink strictly between 0 and 1e27.
setSlopes reverts exactly when the kink is zero, and never reverts for any kink strictly between 0 and 1e27.
For any nonzero asset and any kink strictly between 0 and 1e27, calling setSlopes never reverts.
setSlopes stores the exact slope tuple for an asset and accepted (no-revert) calls leave getVaultAdapterStorage-equivalent nonzero state observable through subsequent successful use.

When setSlopes is called with a valid non-zero kink and correct access, the call succeeds and a subsequent setLimits call with parameter-derived values succeeds, so accepted setLimits parameters do not revert.
setLimits always reverts because the test contract is not authorized (checkAccess(bytes4(0)) fails), so no limits can be changed by an unauthorized caller.
Since the test contract is not the authorized access-control contract for C, any call to setLimits must revert.

property_summary: After setSlopes accepts a valid slope configuration, the interest rate returned by rate is determined by the current utilization and elapsed time, and rate never reverts while the vault reports a non-reverting utilization index.

After accepting valid slopes and limits, calling rate on C (which becomes its own vault/asset) always returns deterministically without reverting, and the returned answer is exactly what a second identical rate call returns when no asset or vault state has changed in between.

Rounding down the utilization rate to 1 when the product of slope0 and utilization divided by kink is 1 keeps the returned rate equal to the floor of slope0*utilization/kink times the multiplier, independent of extra calls to setLimits.

For a valid slope configuration accepted by setSlopes and multiplier/rate limits accepted by setLimits, the interest rate returned by rate is (slope0 * utilization / kink) * minMultiplier / 1e27 when utilization is exactly kink and the multiplier is clamped up to minMultiplier.

For accepted valid slopes with zero slope1 and a zero interest rate, the returned rate when utilization equals kink and the multiplier clamps up to minMultiplier is exactly (slope0 * minMultiplier) / 1e27, provided minMultiplier is set equal to the rate scale (1e27).

For any valid slope data (nonzero kink < 1e27), calling setSlopes emits a SetSlopes event whose asset and slope fields exactly match the submitted parameters, while setLimits with any inputs does not emit a SetSlopes event.

property_summary: After a valid setSlopes call, a subsequent setLimits call must not revert and must not undo or alter the slope data stored for the asset.
After a valid setSlopes call (nonzero kink < 1e27) on an asset, a subsequent setLimits call with any inputs never reverts, so both calls are independently accepted by C.
For any valid slope data (nonzero kink < 1e27) and any limit parameters, setSlopes followed by setLimits never reverts, so both writes are accepted independently.
A valid setSlopes call (nonzero kink < 1e27) never reverts, so the slope write is always accepted for bounded slope parameters.
setSlopes always updates the stored slope data for the given asset, so a subsequent setSlopes with the same asset and different valid slopes must also succeed rather than revert with InvalidKink.
Setting valid slopes for an asset always succeeds and never reverts, regardless of the slope values, as long as kink is nonzero and below 1e27.
For any kink value strictly between 0 and 1e27, calling setSlopes never reverts.
For any asset and any kink strictly between 0 and 1e27, setSlopes with arbitrary slope values never reverts.
For any asset and any strictly-positive kink below 1e27, setSlopes never reverts.
